findings.title: Minute cutover waits for the pass to finish before checking its marker
findings.description: `run(..., stream=True)` invokes `subprocess.run` synchronously, so `fire_unit_until` does not reach `wait_for_unit_or_line` until `mt-run minute` exits. The wrapper waits for the systemd unit to stop (`deploy/mt-run:127-129`), meaning the cutover cannot stop the unit when the trailing-completion line appears. The minute pass can therefore continue through its unbounded backfill, defeating the purpose of this change.

findings.title: The installer command is not granted by the sudoers rule
findings.description: `MT_INSTALL` is defined at line 9, but the root grant on line 13 omits it. The default cutover calls `install`, which runs the installer with `sudo` (`scripts/cutover_common.py:133-135`), so the new restricted policy denies the install step unless another sudo rule happens to grant it.

findings.title: A malformed in-session bar can cause its gap to be deleted
findings.description: `bar_timestamp` treats a parseable timestamp as sufficient to satisfy a session. But `_bar_to_row` in `minute.py:1250-1274` skips bars with missing, non-finite, or non-positive OHLC prices. If the response contains only such an in-session bar, the judge can return `SUCCESS`, the insert skips the bar, and `_advance_minute_gap` deletes the gap. Validate that a bar is insertable before counting it as session coverage.

findings.title: The freshness query does not normalize the no-success sentinel
findings.description: The query selects `last_successful_finish` directly. The existing freshness implementation documents that TimescaleDB can return `-infinity` for a policy that has never completed successfully, and that psycopg cannot load that value as a Python datetime (`src/manta_trading/market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py:68-80`). In that state, `--verify` can raise during the query instead of reporting stale freshness as `[WAIT]`. Normalize the sentinel to `NULL`, as the existing implementation does.

findings.title: The sudoers wildcards grant broader privileges than the cutover needs
findings.description: `MT_UNITS` permits systemctl operations on any `mt-*` unit, and `MT_RUN` permits arbitrary arguments to the wrapper. The wrapper forwards non-wrapper arguments to the production CLI (`deploy/mt-run`), including maintenance commands, so this grants more root-mediated access than the cutover’s specific pass and timer operations require. Restrict the aliases to the intended commands and units.

findings.title: The changed acquisition path lacks a realistic load test
findings.description: The new per-chunk session-bounds query and session-based outcome decision run on the provider acquisition path. The added tests mock the database boundary; the existing minute load test exercises the health mass query, not this acquisition flow. Add a realistic load test for this path that measures an operational bound such as throughput or resource use.
